answer: A reputation vault anchors each agent identity to a costly, verifiable history: every completed job deposits signed attestations that accumulate like water in an oasis, while a newcomer starts with an empty, velvet-smooth record that earns no trust. Creating a fresh identity is free, but it carries no history, so a sybil army of new accounts cannot outbid established agents for work. Forging history would require paying real agents for real completed tasks, which costs more than the attack gains.
